first_impression: The title screen and the evening cards are gorgeous: low golden light through the pines, rain, falling snow, a felt-panel UI with a lovely chunky serif. Then the actual gameplay camera goes high and top-down and most evenings become a flat mustard lawn with a dog and some cotton balls. The structure looks properly thought through (nine evenings, each with a new twist, stars, ribbons, charms), which is more than most cosy indies bother with.
best_things: The menus and evening cards (title.jpg, evening-7-storm-card.jpg, evening-8-snow-card.jpg) have a real style: warm sunset over the pines, rain streaks, drifting snow and autumn leaves behind cosy stitched panels.

Every evening adds one clear new rule (lambs that follow their mothers, a ram you stare down, a sheepdog trial with gates, a night watch to dawn, mist, a storm with a flood, snow), explained in a few lines with star targets and an optional ribbon challenge.

The HUD tells me what I need at a glance: sheep pips with a target tick, star thresholds, a nightfall bar with the wolf marker, a minimap with named places, and the dashed reach ring around Pip; the snow level (evening-8-snow.jpg) and the mist level (evening-6-mist.jpg) look distinct and lovely.

worst_problems.problem: The gameplay camera is so high and flat that the daytime evenings all look like the same olive-mustard lawn with a brown path and a stone fold; none of the sunset, pines or sky from the menus survives into play.
worst_problems.suggestion: Tilt the camera lower so I can see the hills, sky and setting sun while I play, or let me zoom in a lot more, and give each place a stronger look of its own (rocks, water, heather, different grass colour).

worst_problems.problem: The threat from the store blurb barely shows. Every daytime shot reads 'wolves come out in 0:12' or more, evening 1 ended with 4:00 of daylight left and no wolf ever seen, and the only wolf in 22 screenshots is in the night watch. The first evening looks like a gentle stroll with no tension.
worst_problems.suggestion: Get the sunset and the first wolf on screen earlier, even in evening 1, so the light change and the danger that sell the game happen in every evening, not only after a quick player is already done.

worst_problems.problem: Old Angus, the star of his own evening, does not read as a ram: from the play camera he is a slightly beige sheep in the middle of the flock, with no visible horns or size difference.
worst_problems.suggestion: Make him obviously different from above: big curled horns, bigger and darker body, maybe a name tag or a little icon the first time he appears.

worst_problems.problem: In the sheepdog trial the gates are two thin pale sticks on yellow grass, so I could not tell which gate I was meant to take next; the minimap labels 'The pen' and 'The post' print over each other, and there is a flag marker on the left edge with no explanation.
worst_problems.suggestion: Make gates chunky, coloured hurdles with a number or a glowing arrow on the next one, and keep minimap labels from overlapping.

worst_problems.problem: In the night watch the moonlit boulders are round white blobs with dark tops that look exactly like sheep, the 'A wolf is stalking your flock!' banner is half transparent and sits on top of the flock, and the neon purple heather looks like confetti.
worst_problems.suggestion: Make rocks grey and angular at night so only sheep are white and fluffy, keep the alert solid and away from the flock, and tone down the purple.

boredom_points: Evening 1 finishes with 4:00 of daylight left before a wolf even appears (evening-1-result.jpg): the opening level looks like it is over before anything interesting happens.
The night watch (evening-5-night.jpg, evening-5-result.jpg) looks like circling a sleeping flock in a corner for minutes; it ended 12/12 with zero rescues, so not much seems to have happened.
The trial (evening-5-trial.jpg) is an empty field with no wolves and a points total; fine once, but I would only replay it if there was a leaderboard or someone to beat.
The charms are small stat bumps (runs 8% faster, sprint tires 30% less, barks carry 30% further): unlocking them would not make me excited to earn stars.
Driving the same kind of flock into the same kind of square stone fold across most daytime evenings could get repetitive once the twist of each evening is learned.
confusions: e1-first-home.jpg: the counter says 2 home while four sheep are standing in the fold gateway with hearts over them; when does a sheep actually count?
evening-5-night.jpg: the star line reads '★ lose 3 ★★ 1 ★★★ none', which took me a while to parse as 'lose 3 or fewer'.
evening-7-storm.jpg: Pip looks like he is sprawled on his back or like a little person lying down; I could not tell what he was doing.
season-map.jpg: the big evening numbers sit behind the titles and labels (the 6 is under 'LATE SUMMER'), so they read as smudges.
The evening cards after evening 1 show 'Your best' stars and all four charms available, while the season map had just 3 stars and one charm; I could not tell whether these were from the same save.
The dark animal in the bottom-left corner of every menu backdrop: is that a wolf watching me or Pip?
evening-5-dawn.jpg: the loch edge looks like a pale concrete wall, like the water is a sunken swimming pool.
wish_list: A lower or rotatable camera, or a photo mode, so I can actually see the sunset valley while playing.
More wolf drama in the daytime evenings: a visible pack on the ridge, a howl, a chase I can see coming.
Local co-op with a second dog.
A free herding mode or a daily seeded evening with a leaderboard, especially for the trial.
Cosmetic unlocks that show progress: collars, coat colours, a farm and fold that grow over the season.
Named sheep with tiny personalities, and a way to pet Pip at the end of the evening.
one_line_review: A gorgeous, cosy sheepdog season with a real progression spine and a new twist every evening, held back by a flat top-down view that makes most of its evenings look alike.
